title: Delta Cargo partners with New York State to deliver drought relief to Puerto Rico
summary: Working with Governor Kathy Hochul and a network of partners, Delta donated air freight to move nearly 11,000 pounds of drought relief supplies from New York to San Juan.|
body_markdown:
Delta Cargo partnered with New York State, the Afya Foundation and SOMOS to deliver nearly 11,000 pounds of drought relief supplies to Puerto Rico, which has experienced widespread drought conditions this year. Delta donated the air freight, joining forces with Governor Kathy Hochul’s office and the Afya Foundation to move the shipment from New York to Puerto Rico.


"At Delta Cargo, we’re proud to support efforts that make a meaningful difference in the communities we serve. This shipment reflects the best of Delta Cargo and Delta people, and the power of strong partnerships to help ensure critical supplies reach communities that need them most,” said Peter Penseel, President of Delta Cargo


“When our friends and family in Puerto Rico need a helping hand, New York shows up. Grateful to AFYA and Delta for helping make this possible,” Governor Hochul said on social media.


Delta Cargo accepted the shipment at its JFK facility on Nov. 3, and the supplies were loaded onto flights to San Juan that week. They were collected and prepared by the Afya Foundation, a Yonkers-based nonprofit that recovers surplus medical supplies from hospitals in the New York City area.


Following arrival in Puerto Rico, the supplies were distributed in San Juan through the YMCA of Greater New York and Acción Social, in conjunction with the SOMOS Conference Day of Service.


“Thanks to the generosity and collaboration of Delta and our fellow partners, we were able to make a tangible difference in the lives of more than 200 individuals and families throughout Greater San Juan by providing essential food, water and medical supplies. It was a beautiful reminder of what we can accomplish when we come together in service to our communities,” said Sharon Greenberger, President & CEO of the YMCA of Greater New York.


A community’s health and success are defined by neighbors coming together to lift one another up in times of need,” said Senator Jamaal T. Bailey. “The impact of this day of service, delivering essential food pantry items to 200 families and providing vital medical equipment like walkers to those who need it most, is a powerful example of what we can achieve through meaningful partnership. I thank Delta, MSG, the YMCA of San Juan, the YMCA of Greater New York, Acción Social, Youth Justice, and SOMOS for their leadership, coordination, and commitment to delivering these resources directly to our family, friends, and neighbors in Puerto Rico.”


“On behalf of the Somos Inc Board of Directors we are grateful to Delta for being such a consistent corporate partner in our Annual conference in PR,” said Somos Chairman Francisco Diaz.


This is Afya’s second shipment to Puerto Rico in recent months. “Since 2017, Afya has supported communities in Puerto Rico through disasters and everyday medical supply shortages,” said Danielle Butin, Afya’s founder and CEO. “Delta’s generous support is helping us get critical supplies to communities that need them.”


Delta has supported Puerto Rico in times of need before, including a relief flight carrying 20,000 pounds of supplies and water after Hurricane Maria in 2017 and cargo support in partnership with New York State after Hurricane Fiona in 2022.
